title: Dunjunz, official flippy disc (Bug-Byte, 1987), Master 128 side
label: The game
notes: The Master 128 side's files, exported with oaknut from the Master side's HFE flux capture of the 1987 flippy disc (the beeb_hfe archive's Bug Byte, Dunjunz, variant 1, passed to the project by the stardot user Pernod); the eleven machine-code files of the game and its loaders are byte-identical to the NVG archive's Dunjunz.zip, directory 2. The side holds several separate programs, each disassembled on its own: BOOT (BASIC), *DUNJUNZ (Dunjunz, the title screen and loader), Coder2 (the joystick installer), the game, *EDITOR (Editor) and *DEFAULT (Default). The game is this primary listing: Dunj4 (&0E00-&1FFF, the figures above, entered at &0E00 to start a game) is one of five files that make up the resident game with Coder (&0400-&07FE, exec &0740), Dunj3 (&08C0), Dunj5 (&2000) and Dunj2 (&6E80). Four more load into the Master's private RAM (HAZEL): Code (&C500, the joystick handler), Table (&C5A0, level 25, game over, the screen row offsets and the pause key), Code2 (&C700, the music) and Code3 (&D800, a copy of the sprite plotter). The listing saves every file with its DFS load and exec addresses. SHA-256 of each file is in versions/README.md.

disassemblies.label: *DUNJUNZ: title screen and loader
disassemblies.runtime: Dunjunz, load and exec &2649, &913 bytes. Run by BOOT: loads the music, the plotter copy and Table into private RAM, shows the title screen with its twinkling stars, and runs Coder, through Coder2 when a joystick is present.

disassemblies.label: Coder2: joystick installer
disassemblies.runtime: Coder2, load and exec &2000, &26 bytes. Run by *DUNJUNZ when a joystick is present: loads Code (the joystick handler) at &C500, points BYTEV at it and runs Coder.

disassemblies.label: *DEFAULT: level restorer
disassemblies.runtime: Default, load and exec &0E00, &47E0 bytes. Asks for a level number and saves that level's original file, from the copies of all 25 levels it carries, over LevelN on the disc in the drive, undoing the level editor's changes.
